details: U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded approximately $1.26 billion in cumulative net outflows over the past six trading days, marking the steepest weekly drawdown since late January. Similarly, spot Ethereum ETFs experienced their tenth consecutive day of net outflows, indicating a broader reduction in institutional investor risk appetite.
title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $1.26B Outflows; Ethereum Funds Hit 10-Day Streak

details: Ethereum (ETH) dropped to just above $2,000 on May 23, its lowest in nearly two months, following a significant whale sale of 20,000 ETH worth $41.18 million. This adds to the selling pressure from continuous spot ETF outflows. Analysts suggest that a break below the psychological $2,000 level could lead to further declines, though some believe the $1,800 area might attract liquidity before a potential rebound.
title: Ethereum Slides Towards $2,000 Amid Whale Dumps and ETF Outflows

details: A new bipartisan bill, the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026 (ARMA), has been introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives. This bill aims to establish a formal strategic Bitcoin reserve for the government, featuring a 20-year lock-up period for existing holdings and a budget-neutral approach to future accumulation, departing from earlier proposals to acquire 1 million BTC.
title: US Congress Proposes Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill with 20-Year Lock-Up

details: Bitcoin's price experienced fluctuations, initially spiking above $77,000 on May 23 following optimism surrounding potential U.S.-Iran peace talks and active prediction markets. However, it later dropped back towards the $74,000 range due to ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, concerns over U.S. crypto regulation, and broader macroeconomic factors from the Federal Reserve.
title: Bitcoin Volatility as Geopolitical Tensions and Peace Hopes Collide

details: Crypto market analyst Michaël van de Poppe predicts that Bitcoin could decline to the $60,000 level after failing to hold crucial support between $75,000 and $76,000. This bearish outlook is compounded by macroeconomic uncertainty and a prolonged bear market sentiment. However, on-chain data showing 71% of Bitcoin's supply held by long-term investors suggests a break below $60,000 might be unlikely.
title: Analysts Forecast Bitcoin Crash to $60K After Key Support Breaks
